raw_answer_text:
Looking at the validator output, the issue is clear: every `edge` statement needs an **operator** between the two nodes. The operators available are `->`, `<-`, `--`, or `<->`.

For a network topology like this, `--` (undirected connection) is the appropriate choice, since these are bidirectional network links.

Here is the corrected document:

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

node access1 "Access Switch 1"
node access2 "Access Switch 2"
node branch "Branch Router"
node hubprimary "Primary Hub"
node hubbackup "Backup Hub"

edge access1 -- branch
edge access2 -- branch
edge branch -- hubprimary "Primary WAN"
edge branch -- hubbackup "Backup WAN"
```

The only changes made: added the `--` operator to each `edge` statement. This connects the nodes as bidirectional links, which is semantically correct for network topology connections. The labels on the last two edges ("Primary WAN" and "Backup WAN") remain in place and will appear on those links.
